agent_notes: Scope: three debug-log call sites in Model.add_file, Model.remove_file and Model.update_file (src/python/model/model.py lines ~81, ~97, ~112) now pass the filename through sanitize_log_value. A new name is imported from `common`. No public signatures, return values, exceptions or stored state change.

The change only makes logging stricter. The Model's dict keys, its ModelError conditions and the frozen ModelFile all still use the raw file.name and filename. Only the logged string differs. So add, remove and update behave the same for all 10 importers: model/__init__.py, diff.py, controller.py, model_builder.py, auto_queue.py, file_operation_manager.py, extract/dispatch.py, extract/extract_process.py, web/handler/stream_model.py and web/serialize/serialize_model.py.

Import check: sanitize_log_value is re-exported in /Users/julianamacbook/seedsyncarr/src/python/common/__init__.py:1 and defined in /Users/julianamacbook/seedsyncarr/src/python/common/types.py:17. The new `from common import AppError, sanitize_log_value` will not raise ImportError, so model import, and with it the whole controller and web stack, is not at risk at startup.

Type check: sanitize_log_value is typed `value: str`. ModelFile.name and the filename keys are strs, so this path cannot raise a TypeError. If any caller passed a non-str filename to remove_file, the old `'{}'.format()` would have tolerated it but the new call might not. No such caller was found among the listed importers. This is a theoretical edge, not a demonstrated defect.

Behaviour check: C1 characters (0x80 to 0x9F) are deliberately left as-is, as types.py documents, so UTF-8 multibyte filenames log unchanged. Only C0 control characters and DEL are escaped. Operators grepping debug logs for filenames that really contain those characters will see escaped forms such as \n and \x1b. That is the intended result.

Performance: `.format()` runs before logger.debug, so the sanitize work is done even when DEBUG is off. This was already true of the formatting before the change. The extra cost is one linear pass over a short filename per model mutation. Model updates follow the LFTP and scanner polling rate, so the overhead is negligible even with thousands of files. Lazy `%s` formatting would avoid it, but that is optional.

No database, schema, migration, serialization or API-surface implications. Worst case if sanitize_log_value had a bug is a garbled or raised debug log line inside a model mutation, which would abort that add, remove or update. Given the str-typed inputs and the simple escaping, this is very unlikely. The unit tests in test_model/test_model.py (commit 7035477, RED) cover these three sites.
Verdict: no blocking issues on the impact axis; the change can ship as-is.
